# Pillar

## What it means

A pillar is one of the five things that happen in an [AI Space](./ai-space.md):

- [Specifying](./specifying.md): writing down what is wanted, and agreeing it, before it is built.
- [Planning](./planning.md): deciding what to build, in what order, and who is building it now.
- [Working](./working.md): a session doing the work.
- [Producing](./producing.md): what the work produces, which is the payloads and the agreed specs.
- [Shaping](./shaping.md): the Human Lead deciding how the Space works, by writing and changing the Lore.

A session can be in any pillar at any moment, and the Human Lead can ask any session to do something that belongs to any of them. Every session follows the Lore, whichever pillar it is in.

The pillars say what happens in a Space. The [layers](./layer.md) say where the way of doing each of these things comes from.

## Where it is kept

A pillar is not a file or a folder. The card of a verb, of a process and of a contract names its pillar in the key `pillar` of its frontmatter, with one of the values `specifying`, `planning`, `working`, `producing` and `shaping`.

## What acts on it

No verb acts on a pillar. The default set ships one process for each of three pillars: specify for Specifying, plan for Planning and work for Working. Producing and Shaping have no process.
